title: Register on prospective evaluation of therapy-free remission in chronic myeloid leukaemia with the aim of identifying prognostic factors
summary:
Nowadays, the standard of treatment for chronic myeloid leukaemia (CML) is the use of tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs), which were developed only about 20 years ago. These highly potent TKIs selectively inhibit the biological mechanisms in the body that lead to the production of leukaemia cells. 

It was only about 10 years ago when it was shown that in many patients who responded very well to several years of TKI therapy, the body does not restart the production of leukaemia cells even after discontinuation of the TKI, so that drug therapy can be discontinued for years or perhaps even forever.  

However, in about 40-50% of those who have stopped, the proportion of leukaemia cells in the blood increases so high, usually in the first 6 months, that - in order not to risk a disease progression - the TKI therapy has to be resumed.   

The reasons why only less than half of those who discontinue therapy are able to maintain it in the long term have not yet been clearly explained. The body's own immune defence probably plays an important role, but other factors that have not yet been proven, such as the different modes of action of the TKIs or changes in the genome, may also have an influence.

For this research project, adults with CML who are planning to discontinue TKI treatment in the short-term with the aim of being free of therapy will be asked whether they consent to the collection of data relating to the outcome of their discontinuation attempt. 

From the time of consent until the end of the study (expected to be 31 May 2028), data will then be ...

....by the attending physician, data (e.g. examination results) on the outcome after discontinuation of the CML drug will be regularly recorded in an electronic study database. In addition, past data on the history of CML and its treatment since diagnosis as well as on the general health condition are collected. 

.... participants are asked to complete a 4-page questionnaire on their health-related quality of life before stopping the CML medication and every 6 months thereafter. This should not require more than 15 minutes.  

The data will only be recorded in coded form in the study database. Coding means that all personal data that could identify the participants (name, date of birth, address, etc.) are replaced by a code (= are pseudonymised).

The research project was initiated by the University of Heidelberg, represented by the Mannheim Medical Faculty. It is being carried out at numerous clinics and practices in Germany. The project only serves to gain knowledge; no commercial interests are being pursued.

Usually, blood samples are taken regularly for disease control after discontinuation of the TKI and the proportion of leukaemia cells in the blood are determined. Participants in this registry will also be asked whether they agree that 
a small amount of blood from these samples be taken and stored in a "biomaterial bank" in the scientific laboratory of the Clinic for Haematology Mannheim for later investigation. 
The same applies to bone marrow taken for examination. 

This biomaterial collection should be used for further investigations with regard to the research question of this project. In this case, the results of the blood tests might be evaluated together with the data from this research project. 

With the hoped-for gain in knowledge, the chances of lasting treatment freedom for all CML patients should be improved.

interventions.name: Patients >18 years  discontinue CML treatment outside of clinical (interventional) trials with the aim of maintaining treatment-free remission, if applicable also subsequently after participation in the PONTrack study.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. informed written consent of the patient(s).
2. Only adult patients (≥ 18 years)
3. confirmed diagnosis of Philadelphia chromosome and / or BCR-ABL1 fusion gene positive chronic myeloid leukaemia (CML) 
4. treatment of CML with a tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) in first-line or multi-line, mono- or combined therapy
5. intention to discontinue TKI treatment at the time of entry into the register with the aim of treatment-free remission (for the first time or repeated after previous failed discontinuation attempts). 
6. commitment of the participating institution to send all blood samples collected during routine care for the determination of the molecular remission level to the scientific laboratory of the Universitätsmedizin Mannheim for analysis and for the biomaterial database for the duration of the patient's participation in the register. For these samples, the amount of blood to be collected must be increased by 10-30 ml for the scientific analyses.Written informed consent from the patient is required for use in the register.
Exclusion criteria:
none
